purpose: Independent downstream PLACE rolls conditioned on already-resolved cause/detail. Event setting and terminal place are kept semantically distinct in metadata but rendered through one compact PLACE field.
probability_semantics: Each distribution is conditional on the trigger cause and country/profile shown. Source counts/percentages are normalized only within the stated source population. PLACE never changes mortality, cause, cause detail, suicide context, X80 location, X41 drug class, or seasonality.

FI.label: Finland | accidental drowning event setting
FI.provenance: Safety Investigation Authority Finland S1/2010Y, all 228 accidental water-related deaths investigated 1 Apr 2010-31 Mar 2011: lake 110, sea 51, river 22, pond 14, indoor pool 5, remaining 26 in smaller waters such as ditches/brooks/bogs and bathtubs. Counts are rolled directly after normalization.

CA.label: Canada | unintentional drowning event setting
CA.provenance: Lifesaving Society / Drowning Prevention Research Centre Canada, 2024 Canadian Detailed Drowning Report, national 2015-2019 water-related fatality distribution: lake/pond 35%, river 26%, bathtub 13%, pool 9%, ocean 6%, other 11%.

sources.title: S1/2010Y Deaths by Drowning in Finland 1.4.2010-31.3.2011
2024 Canadian Detailed Drowning Report
sources.publisher: Lifesaving Society / Drowning Prevention Research Centre Canada

icd_constraints.provenance: ICD-10 W65/W66 explicitly identifies a bathtub setting; no statistical water-setting roll is needed.
ICD-10 W67/W68 explicitly identifies a swimming-pool setting; no statistical water-setting roll is needed.

The resolved ICD context requires natural/open water. The country distribution is therefore renormalized across source categories that are explicitly compatible with natural/open water; mixed or unspecified residual categories are excluded rather than guessed.
icd_constraints.model_status: Country-native distribution constrained by resolved ICD environment

male.provenance: European Homicide Monitor, Finland 2003-2006, Table 7, male victims: 350 valid known-location cases. Source counts used directly; 5 unknown-location cases excluded from the conditional known-place roll.

female.provenance: European Homicide Monitor, Finland 2003-2006, Table 8, female victims: 136 valid known-location cases. Source counts used directly.

sources.title: Homicide in Finland, the Netherlands and Sweden: A First Study on the European Homicide Monitor Data
sources.use: Tables 7-8, Finland homicide locations by victim sex

FI.label: Finland | fatal road setting
FI.provenance: European Commission/CARE National Road Safety Profile Finland, 2020 road fatalities: 68% rural roads, 28% urban roads, 4% motorways.

CA.label: Canada | fatal collision setting
CA.provenance: Transport Canada, Canadian Motor Vehicle Traffic Collision Statistics 2023, Number of Collisions by Location: 799 urban fatal collisions, 932 rural, 37 not stated, total 1,768. Counts used directly.

sources.title: Canadian Motor Vehicle Traffic Collision Statistics: 2023

FI.label: Finland | cancer place of death
FI.provenance: Ahtiluoto et al. nationwide Finnish 2019 register cohort: among cancer decedents, place of death was hospital 82.1%, home 11.0%, long-term care facility 6.8%. Percentages are normalized for rounding.

CA.label: Canada | cancer place of death
CA.provenance: CIHI End-of-Life Hospital Care for Cancer Patients, citing Canadian Partnership Against Cancer analysis of Statistics Canada data for 2005-2009: approximately 70% of cancer deaths occurred in hospital and 11% at home. The remaining 19% is an explicit derived residual covering other/unspecified settings; it is not split further.

sources.title: Impact of specialist palliative care on utilization of healthcare and social services at the end-of-life: a nationwide register-based cohort study
End-of-Life Hospital Care for Cancer Patients

FI.label: Finland | neurodegenerative place of death
FI.provenance: Ahtiluoto et al. nationwide Finnish 2019 register cohort: neurodegenerative decedents died in hospital 43.2%, at home 7.0%, and in long-term care 49.7%. Percentages are normalized for rounding. Trigger code family follows the Finnish life-limiting neurodegenerative grouping used in related register work.

sources.title: Impact of specialist palliative care on utilization of healthcare and social services at the end-of-life: a nationwide register-based cohort study
